topics.title: U.S. General Insurance Products and Coverages
topics.objective: The candidate will understand the different types of general insurance products and coverages offered in the United States.

outcomes.text: Describe the contents of the ISO Personal Auto Policy (PAP) and the ISO Homeowners (HO) policies and the coverages they provide.
Explain how insurable interest, policy provisions for valuing losses, and insurance to value affect a loss payment amount under property insurance.
Describe commercial property insurance in terms of categories of loss exposures.
Describe the contents of the ISO commercial property (CP) and general liability (CGL) policies, and types of coverage they provide.
Identify the factors that affect commercial insurance premiums and how premium is determined.
Describe commercial auto insurance in terms of the loss exposures.
Describe the contents of the ISO Commercial Automobile policies and the coverages they provide.
Describe the workers compensation (WC) system.
Explain why employers liability insurance is needed and how the ISO WC and Employers Liability Insurance Policy address this need.
Explain how premium bases, classifications, and premium adjustments affect WC insurance.
Describe various specialty insurance coverages (including excess liability, umbrella liability, professional liability, cyber risk, surety and terrorism).

topics.title: U.S. General Insurance Regulation
topics.objective: The candidate will understand the development and structure of insurance regulations in the United States.

outcomes.text: Describe the functions of key regulatory bodies in the U.S. including the NAIC and SEC.
Describe the historical development of general insurance regulations in the United States.
Describe and interpret the current state of general insurance regulations in the United States.
Summarize the regulatory activities of state insurance departments, including insurance commissioners’ duties.
Describe the licensing requirements for insurers and insurance personnel in the United States.
Describe the methods that U.S. regulators use to maintain the solvency of insurers.

topics.title: U.S. GI Financial Reporting and Financial Health Measurement
topics.objective: The candidate will understand the different reporting standards for U.S. general insurance companies and use statutory financial statement information to measure insurer financial health.

outcomes.text: Demonstrate knowledge of U.S. GAAP, U.S. statutory accounting and U.S. tax accounting for general insurance companies.
Describe the elements of the NAIC Annual Statement.
Complete and interpret NAIC Annual Statement pages/schedules (as referenced in the resources).
Evaluate the financial health of a U.S. general insurer using the Annual Statement (e.g., NAIC RBC and IRIS Ratios).

topics.title: Responsibilities of a U.S. Signing General Insurance Actuary
topics.objective: The candidate will be able to use applicable standards of practice to carry out the responsibilities of a U.S. signing general insurance actuary as defined by regulators and the American Academy of Actuaries.

outcomes.text: Describe and apply the concept of materiality.
Describe, interpret and apply the applicable U.S. Standards of Practice.
Describe, interpret and apply the responsibilities of a signing actuary with respect to the U.S. Statement of Actuarial Opinion and the Actuarial Report.
